items.title: 68239_Ram Ramirez oral history interview
items.q: there was a gentleman by the name of Eydan(?), who came from Amsterdam Avenue and 106th Street

ctx.x: band to play St. Regis. I was in Europe when that happened. But prior to that, it was back in the Thirties, the early Thirties, about '31 or '32, Billy Hicks, Joe Vidas(?), Quinton Harrington and...

By the way, he's supposed to write me a letter and tell me the exact year, exactly... He took a band to Haiti. And in Haiti there was a gentleman by the name of Eydan(?), who came from Amsterdam Avenue and 106th Street, somewhere around that way, who put up the first electric sign in Haiti. It was a little small theatre right in the park, in the little rotunda, a little round place where the band used to play. It was at a little bungalow which they called the first theatre in Port Au Prince, the first motion…

And I can remind you, that's the beginning of the hill at Port Au Prince... Their market is at the bottom of the hill. All around it's like a mountain, and all this housing surrounds, like, the valley which is the center(?) of the palace, see. You take a little cab in those days... Port Au Prince was poor, and thanks to the generosity of Uncle Sam, they help everybody else but people in their hemisphere they have never tried to... But anyway, the denomination of their money was a gor(?), they call it -- it's…
